model.name: Concept / Term
model.purpose: Govern the lifecycle, decision authority, provenance, evidence and quality of a stable semantic concept whose identity is independent of any label, so an agent can propose, approve, publish, version, deprecate, merge, split, retire and audit a concept record without conflating that governance with the mutable designations, definitions and mappings attached to it.
model.scope_statement: This pass covers only the governance, lifecycle, evidence and quality plane of WM-KNW-006, plus the merged service layers for the whole model. The concept is the stable, label-independent unit of thought that carries identity; designations, definitions and mapping assertions are mutable attachments governed through, but not defined by, this pass.
in_scope: Registration state set, permitted transitions and the authority required for each transition
Proposal, review, approval, publication, deprecation and retirement workflow with recorded decisions
Version designation, release binding, change classification and immutable-release guarantees
Atomic change history, append-only governance records and point-in-time reconstruction
Authoritative external source of a definition, adoption or derivation relationship, and source drift
Warrant and rationale evidence supporting the concept's existence and scope, held by reference
Declaration of applicable constraint sets and retention of the resulting conformance report
Editorial completeness, maturity and quality measurement of the concept record
Duplicate candidacy, merge, split, redirect and never-reuse of retired identifiers
Ownership, stewardship, namespace and identifier stewardship, rights, embargo, retention and disposition instructions
out_of_scope: Structure of designations, labels, language tags and definition text (WM-KNW-006 lexical core split)
Semantic relation predicates, match-strength semantics and mapping-set composition (WM-KNW-006 relation split)
Concept scheme membership, top concepts and scheme-level boundaries (parent model WM-KNW-002)
Execution of validation: shape languages, evaluation algorithms and validation-engine behaviour
Audit-log storage, tamper-evident ledger protocols and security monitoring semantics
Policy evaluation and enforcement of licences or access rules at runtime
Scheduling, approval and physical execution of destruction under a retention schedule
Identity, contact data and organisational lifecycle of the agents who act as steward or authority
Indexing, search ranking and retrieval behaviour of any system that consumes the concept
Jurisdiction-specific legal determinations about personal data, copyright or database rights

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-KNW-006 lexical core structures (designation, label, language tag, definition text, ct-core-usage-attestation)
boundary_notes.distinction: This pass governs registration, decisions, versions and evidence status of the stable concept. It never redefines designation structure, label typing, language tagging or attestation content; it carries designation references and the publication access exception only.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-KNW-006 semantic relation and mapping structures (ct-rel-art-mapping-set, ct-rel-art-crosswalk-specification, ct-rel-art-interchange-package)
boundary_notes.distinction: Relation predicates, match strength, scheme-pair binding and export-closure composition are defined there. This pass supplies only the change classification, decision and validation gates a mapping change must pass.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-KNW-002 parent concept scheme / knowledge organization system
boundary_notes.distinction: Scheme membership, top concepts, scheme-level release identity and scheme boundaries belong to the parent. This pass governs an individual concept record's state within a bound scheme release.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Constraint evaluation engine (for example a SHACL processor)
boundary_notes.distinction: This model owns the declaration that a constraint set version applies and the retained conformance report reference. It does not own evaluation, execution, or the engine's conformance semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Enterprise audit log, tamper-evident ledger or security monitoring service
boundary_notes.distinction: This model requires append-only governance records carrying event, effective and ingestion times. It does not define audit-trail storage, log integrity protocols or monitoring semantics, and a reference to an external audit record confers no ownership of those.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Records management and disposition execution authority
boundary_notes.distinction: This model carries a retention class reference, legal-hold flag and tombstone requirement. Scheduling, hold release and destruction are executed by the adopting Dimension's records authority.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Rights and licence policy model with its policy evaluator
boundary_notes.distinction: This model carries the licence or policy reference and subject-specific constraint parameters. Policy interpretation, evaluation and enforcement remain with the policy model and its evaluator.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Defines skos:Concept as a label-independent unit of thought, notation, concept schemes, mapping properties and the documentation properties (definition, scopeNote, editorialNote, historyNote, changeNote). Section 4.6.1 states a scheme boundary cannot be closed. It contains no versioning or status vocabulary, which is why status and version machinery is sourced elsewhere.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent, wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasRevisionOf, wasAttributedTo, actedOnBehalfOf, generatedAtTime and invalidatedAtTime, plus the qualified-influence pattern. Grounds provenance, derivation, attribution and delegation for governance events.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.relevance: dcat:version, previousVersion, hasVersion, hasCurrentVersion, versionNotes, status and dcterms:replaces establish version chains; prov:qualifiedAttribution with dcat:hadRole grounds role-qualified attribution for stewards and authorities.

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices
sources.relevance: BP4 licensing, BP5 provenance, BP6 quality, BP7 version indicator, BP8 complete version history, BP9 persistent URI, BP10 URI reuse, BP11 URIs for versions and series, BP27 preserve identifiers. Directly grounds versioning, provenance, licensing, quality and identifier persistence requirements.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.relevance: ValidationReport with sh:conforms, ValidationResult with focusNode, resultPath, sourceShape and resultSeverity (Violation/Warning/Info), and the shapes-graph versus data-graph separation. Grounds the validation report artifact and the blocking-versus-advisory severity split without claiming ownership of evaluation.

sources.title: Data Quality Vocabulary (DQV)
sources.relevance: QualityMeasurement, Metric, Dimension, Category, QualityAnnotation, QualityCertificate and QualityPolicy, aligned to PROV and DCAT. Grounds editorial quality measurement as dimension-plus-metric rather than an opaque score. It is a Note, not a Recommendation.

sources.title: DCMI Metadata Terms
sources.relevance: license, accessRights, rightsHolder, provenance, created, issued, modified, valid, replaces, isReplacedBy, source and bibliographicCitation. Grounds rights, access, custody-change provenance, effective validity and supersession pointers.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines full-date T full-time with mandatory seconds and a required time-offset of Z or a numeric offset, and defines -00:00 as the unknown-local-offset form. Grounds the timestamp rule and the local prohibition on -00:00.

sources.title: RFC 8785: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)
sources.relevance: Deterministic property ordering by UTF-16 code unit, ECMAScript number serialisation and defined string escaping, so hashing and signing are reliably repeatable. Grounds the canonical-form and digest re-derivation rules for structured artifacts.

sources.title: ANSI/NISO Z39.19-2005 (R2010) Guidelines for the Construction, Format, and Management of Monolingual Controlled Vocabularies
sources.relevance: Scope covers contents, display, construction, testing, maintenance and management of controlled vocabularies, including term warrant and vocabulary maintenance. Full normative clauses are behind purchase, so detailed maintenance rules are cited as scope only.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 11179-6:2023 Information technology — Metadata registries (MDR) — Part 6: Registration
sources.relevance: Defines information, conditions and procedures for registering administered items, distinguishes lifecycle from documentation registration status categories, requires all mandatory attributes and associations for Recorded, requires steward sponsorship plus registration-authority approval to reach Qualified or higher, and requires retirement procedures. Full text is paywalled; the catalogue record and standards-body summaries were used.

sources.title: ISO 25964 — the international standard for thesauri and interoperability with other vocabularies
sources.version_or_date: ISO 25964-1:2011 and ISO 25964-2:2013; maintenance-agency page accessed 2026-09-02
sources.relevance: Data model separating ThesaurusConcept from ThesaurusTerm, creation and modification timestamps, historyNote, VersionHistory, and a published SKOS correspondence at purl.org/iso25964/skos-thes. Grounds concept-versus-term separation and version history for thesaurus maintenance.

sources.title: OBO Foundry Principle 4: Versioning
sources.relevance: Each release must have a resolvable version IRI whose identifier string matches the artifact, versioned PURLs must resolve in perpetuity, and the content of released files MUST NOT be changed — bugs are fixed in a new release. Grounds immutable releases and durable version resolution.

sources.title: Obsoleting an Existing Ontology Term (OBO Academy / OBOOK)
sources.relevance: owl:deprecated marking, OBSOLETE label prefix, IAO:0100001 term-replaced-by for successors, oboInOwl:consider for advisory alternatives, obsolescence-reason IRIs including terms-merged and term-split, and the rule that identifiers are never deleted or reused. Grounds deprecation, merge, split and redirect handling.

sources.title: Asset Description Metadata Schema (ADMS)
sources.version_or_date: W3C Working Group Note 1 August 2013; retired August 2023, maintained by SEMIC
sources.relevance: adms:status pointing at a SKOS-controlled workflow status, adms:prev/next/last version chain and adms:versionNotes describing changes between versions. Its retirement as a W3C Note is recorded as a conflict/drift risk.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Policy (Set, Offer, Agreement), Permission, Prohibition, Duty, Constraint with temporal and spatial refinements, Asset, Party and Action. Grounds machine-readable licence, embargo and access constraints carried as references without local enforcement.

sources.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
sources.relevance: MAJOR for incompatible changes, MINOR for backward-compatible additions, PATCH for backward-compatible fixes, RFC 2119 keywords, and the rule that a released version's contents MUST NOT be modified. Used as a de facto convention for change classification, with its API orientation recorded as a conflict.

bundles.name: Concept lifecycle, decision authority and change control
bundles.description: How a concept record enters the register, moves between governed states under a named authority, is bound to releases, and accumulates an immutable change history including merge, split and redirect.
bundles.rationale: SKOS defines the concept but supplies no status or versioning vocabulary, so registration status, workflow authority and version chains must be sourced from registration and cataloguing standards and modelled explicitly on the stable concept rather than on any label.

layers.name: Registration states, authority and retirement
layers.description: The governed state set, who may move a record between states, and how a concept leaves active use without its identifier ever being reused.

findings.name: Registration state model and transition rules
findings.description: The enumerated states a concept record may occupy, split into lifecycle states (development and usage preference) and documentation states (no further development), with entry criteria, permitted transitions and the meaning each state guarantees to consumers.

questions.text: Which registration states may this concept record occupy, and which are lifecycle states rather than documentation-only states?
answer_data: Registration status code and its governing code system
Status category flag: lifecycle or documentation

questions.text: What mandatory attributes and associations must be complete before the record may progress beyond the recorded state?
answer_data: Completeness criteria set per target state
Unsatisfied criteria list at the time of evaluation

questions.text: Which role must authorise each transition, and which transitions are irreversible?
answer_data: Transition-to-required-role matrix
Irreversibility flag and statement of authorisation

questions.text: What stability guarantee does each state give a downstream consumer about the concept's meaning?
answer_data: Per-state consumer guarantee statement
Whether the state permits definition-scope change

data_elements.name: Registration status
data_elements.description: Coded state of the concept record within the registration authority's workflow.

data_elements.name: Status category
data_elements.description: Whether the status is a lifecycle category or a documentation category.

data_elements.name: Statement of authorisation
data_elements.description: The recorded basis on which the current status was conferred, naming the authorising body.

data_elements.name: Permitted transition set
data_elements.description: Allowed next states from the current state, each with its required role and reversibility flag.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The state model is a governed enumeration plus a transition matrix. It is reference data resolved against a code system and a role registry, carries no payload, and would be falsified rather than supported by materialising it as a document; the decision that moved the record is captured separately as a decision record.

findings.name: Decision authority and proposal workflow
findings.description: Who holds decision authority over this concept, the proposal-review-approval steps a change must pass, and the auditable record of each governed decision including dissent and appeal.

questions.text: Who holds decision authority over this concept, and under what documented mandate?
answer_data: Decision body identifier and mandate reference
Scope of authority: which change classes it may approve

questions.text: What proposal, review and approval steps must a change pass before publication?
answer_data: Ordered workflow step list with required role per step
Step outcome and completion event time

questions.text: What evidence, options considered and dissent must a decision capture to remain auditable?
answer_data: Considered options with rationale for the chosen one
Recorded dissent, abstention or minority position

questions.text: How is a contested or appealed decision recorded without rewriting the original decision?
answer_data: Appeal reference and superseding decision identifier
Supersession pointer on the original, which remains readable

data_elements.name: Decision body reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party or committee holding authority for the decision class.

data_elements.name: Role-qualified attribution
data_elements.description: Agent reference plus the role in which the agent acted for this decision.

data_elements.name: Decision outcome
data_elements.description: Coded outcome of the governed decision, such as approved, rejected, deferred or withdrawn.

data_elements.name: Superseded decision reference
data_elements.description: Pointer from a later decision to the decision it replaces, leaving the original intact.

artifacts.name: Concept governance decision record
artifacts.description: Immutable record of one governed decision about this concept: the question put, options considered, outcome, role-qualified participants, dissent, and the event and effective times.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Concept-scoped serial: concept identifier as scope discriminator plus a never-reused integer sequence dedicated to decision records; if the registration authority's case-management system already assigns a decision key, that authoritative master-system identifier takes priority and the serial becomes a secondary local reference.

findings.name: Deprecation, retirement and succession
findings.description: Grounds for deprecating rather than correcting a concept, the successor relationship offered to clients, the guarantee that a retired identifier is never reused or repointed, and how long resolution is promised.

questions.text: On what grounds may this concept be deprecated instead of corrected in place?
answer_data: Coded obsolescence reason, for example merged, split, out of scope or placeholder removed
Narrative justification and the deciding authority reference

questions.text: Which successor concept replaces the deprecated concept, and is the replacement authoritative or merely advisory?
answer_data: Authoritative replacement reference, zero or one
Advisory alternative references, zero to many

questions.text: What must a client still holding the deprecated identifier do, and until when is resolution guaranteed?
answer_data: Client migration instruction and target
Resolution guarantee end instant or an explicit perpetual commitment

questions.text: How is a retired identifier prevented from ever being reused or repointed to a different meaning?
answer_data: Tombstone record retained in the namespace register
Minting-service exclusion entry for the retired identifier

data_elements.name: Deprecated flag
data_elements.description: Boolean marking that the concept is no longer in active use, independent of whether a successor exists.

data_elements.name: Obsolescence reason
data_elements.description: Coded reason for obsolescence, distinguishing merge, split, scope removal and placeholder removal.

data_elements.name: Replaced by
data_elements.description: Authoritative successor concept reference that consumers should substitute.

data_elements.name: Advisory alternatives
data_elements.description: Non-authoritative candidate concepts offered where no exact successor exists.

artifacts.name: Concept deprecation notice
artifacts.description: Published notice that a concept has been deprecated or retired, carrying the obsolescence reason, successor or advisory alternatives, client migration instruction, resolution guarantee and effective instant.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Concept-scoped serial: concept identifier as scope discriminator plus a never-reused integer sequence dedicated to deprecation notices, so a re-deprecation after reinstatement produces a new number rather than overwriting the first.

layers.name: Versioning, change history and duplicate resolution
layers.description: How a concept record's state is bound to an immutable release, how every change is recorded append-only with cause and time, and how duplicates are detected and resolved by merge, split or redirect.

findings.name: Version designation and release binding
findings.description: Which immutable release of the owning scheme a governed record state belongs to, how a change is classified as editorial, additive or breaking, and how a version designation stays distinct from record identity.

questions.text: Which immutable release of the owning concept scheme does this governed record state belong to?
answer_data: Release identifier and its resolvable version IRI
Record state digest as published in that release

questions.text: How is a proposed change classified as editorial, additive or breaking, and who performs that classification?
answer_data: Change class code and the classification rule applied
Classifying agent reference and role

questions.text: What guarantees that a published release remains unaltered and retrievable at a later date?
answer_data: Immutability commitment statement and its custodian
Retained release digest with algorithm, mode and mode version

questions.text: How does a version designation relate to, and remain distinct from, the concept record identifier?
answer_data: Concept identifier that is stable across all releases
Version designation string, which may be date-formed but is never identity

data_elements.name: Bound release reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the scheme release in which this record state was published.

data_elements.name: Version designation
data_elements.description: Human-facing version label for the release, which may use a date form but never serves as identity.

data_elements.name: Change class
data_elements.description: Coded classification of the change as editorial, additive or breaking.

data_elements.name: Previous version reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the immediately preceding published state of this concept, forming the version chain.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Release binding and change classification are pointers and codes on the concept record; the release artifact itself is owned by the parent scheme model and the interchange package is owned by the relation split, so materialising a local artifact here would duplicate a neighbour's payload.

findings.name: Change history, event timing and audit trail
findings.description: Append-only atomic change records with the causing activity, agent and decision, separated event, effective and ingestion times, and the ability to reconstruct the record as it stood at any past instant.

questions.text: What atomic change was made, to which element of the concept record, and from what prior value?
answer_data: Changed element path with prior and new canonical values
Pre-image digest of the record before the change

questions.text: Which activity, agent and prior decision caused this change?
answer_data: Causing activity reference and its agent attribution
Referenced decision record identifier

questions.text: When did the change occur, when does it take effect, and when was it ingested into this register?
answer_data: Event time, effective time and ingestion time as separate values
Whether effective time is prospective or retrospective

questions.text: How can a consumer reconstruct this concept record exactly as it stood at an arbitrary past instant?
answer_data: Ordered change sequence with inverse operations
Verifiable digest of each reconstructed state

questions.text: How is an erroneous change record corrected without deleting or rewriting history?
answer_data: Correcting change record with a pointer to the erroneous one
Non-destructive annotation marking the original as superseded

data_elements.name: Change operation
data_elements.description: Typed, reversible operation over a semantic path: add, replace, remove or move, with prior and new values.

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the governed act actually occurred, as RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Effective time
data_elements.description: Instant from which the change takes effect for consumers, which may differ from the event time.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the register captured or received the record of the change.

data_elements.name: Pre-image digest
data_elements.description: Digest of the canonical record state immediately before the change, used for conflict detection.

artifacts.name: Concept change record
artifacts.description: Immutable, append-only record of one accepted change to a concept record, carrying reversible operations, pre-image digest, causing activity and decision references, and separated event, effective and ingestion times.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Concept-scoped serial: concept identifier as scope discriminator plus a never-reused integer sequence dedicated to change records, giving a total order of changes per concept independent of clock skew between contributing systems.

findings.name: Duplicate candidacy, merge, split and redirect
findings.description: Evidence by which another record is judged to denote the same concept, which identifier survives a merge, how a split disambiguates inbound references, and how automated duplicate signals are bounded.

questions.text: By what evidence is another record judged to denote the same unit of thought as this one?
answer_data: Sameness evidence set: definition comparison, notation, shared authoritative source
Confidence statement and the reviewing agent

questions.text: Which identifier survives a merge, and how are the non-surviving identifiers redirected?
answer_data: Surviving concept identifier and the survivorship rule applied
Redirect entries from each non-surviving identifier to the survivor

questions.text: When a concept is split, how are prior usages and inbound references disambiguated across the successors?
answer_data: Successor concept identifiers with their delimited scopes
Disposition rule for inbound references that cannot be resolved automatically

questions.text: Which automated duplicate-candidate signals are used, and what false-positive tolerance is accepted before human review?
answer_data: Signal list with score and threshold per signal
Required human confirmation step and its role

data_elements.name: Duplicate candidate
data_elements.description: Reference to another concept record proposed as denoting the same concept, with signal scores.

data_elements.name: Merge survivorship rule
data_elements.description: Rule and its outcome determining which identifier survives, such as earliest registration or widest external adoption.

data_elements.name: Redirect entry
data_elements.description: Directed mapping from a non-surviving or split-source identifier to one or more successors.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Merge, split and redirect outcomes are structural pointers held on the concept records themselves and are published through the deprecation notice and change record already declared elsewhere in this bundle; adding a separate merge artifact would duplicate those payloads and create a second, competing source of truth for successor resolution.

bundles.name: Provenance, evidence, validation and editorial quality
bundles.description: Where the concept's meaning comes from, what warrant justifies it, which constraint sets it is checked against, and how editorially complete and mature the record is.
bundles.rationale: Best practice requires complete origin information, quality information and fitness statements alongside the data itself; validation reports and quality measurements give falsifiable assurance rather than an unevidenced conformance claim.

layers.name: Authoritative sources and evidentiary warrant
layers.description: The external authority for the concept's definition, the derivation relationship to it, and the warrant that justifies admitting the concept at all.

findings.name: Authoritative source and derivation provenance
findings.description: Which external source is authoritative for this concept's definition and at which version, whether the concept is originated, adopted verbatim, adapted or derived, and how later change or withdrawal of that source is reflected.

questions.text: Which external source is authoritative for this concept's definition, and at what version or publication date?
answer_data: Source reference with citation and version or date
Locator or clause within the source

questions.text: Is this concept originated locally, adopted verbatim, adapted, or derived from another vocabulary?
answer_data: Derivation mode code
Derivation link to the upstream concept where one exists

questions.text: Which agent asserted the current definition, and on whose behalf did that agent act?
answer_data: Asserting agent reference and role
Delegating organisation reference

questions.text: How is a later change to, or withdrawal of, the authoritative source reflected in this record?
answer_data: Source-monitoring commitment and review interval
Triggered change class when the source changes materially

data_elements.name: Authoritative source reference
data_elements.description: Citation and identifier of the source that is authoritative for the definition, with its version or date.

data_elements.name: Derivation mode
data_elements.description: Coded relationship to the upstream source: originated, adopted, adapted or derived.

data_elements.name: Custody and ownership-change statement
data_elements.description: Narrative of changes in ownership and custody significant for authenticity and interpretation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Authoritative-source provenance is a set of outbound citations and derivation pointers to resources held and versioned by their own publishers. Copying source text locally would create an uncontrolled and rapidly stale replica and could breach the source licence; the reference plus version binding is the defensible representation.

findings.name: Warrant and rationale evidence
findings.description: The governance-grade evidence set justifying that this is a distinct unit of thought with the scope claimed, held by reference to retained attestations and citations rather than restated locally.

questions.text: What warrant justifies admitting this as a distinct concept rather than a variant of an existing one?
answer_data: Warrant type: literary, organisational or user warrant
Distinguishing criterion against the nearest existing concept

questions.text: Which retained attestations and citations support the current definition, and where are they held?
answer_data: References to retained usage attestations held by the lexical core structures
Holding system identifier and retrieval path for each item

questions.text: What counter-evidence or rejected alternative scoping was considered, and why was it set aside?
answer_data: Rejected scoping options with reasons
Reference to the decision record that resolved the question

questions.text: When supporting evidence cannot be published, what minimal defensible reference is exposed instead?
answer_data: Restricted-reference stub with holding system and access route
Redaction or minimisation note, without the restricted content itself

data_elements.name: Warrant type
data_elements.description: Coded basis for admitting the concept: literary, organisational or user warrant.

data_elements.name: Evidence reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to a retained attestation or citation supporting the definition, with its holding system.

data_elements.name: Evidence disclosure state
data_elements.description: Whether each evidence item is publishable, restricted or embargoed, and the basis recorded for that state.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The retained evidence payloads are usage attestations owned by the lexical core structures under ct-core-usage-attestation. This finding carries only warrant typing, evidence pointers and disclosure state; declaring a local evidence artifact would duplicate an adjacent split's artifact and split custody of the same material.

layers.name: Validation, conformance and editorial quality
layers.description: Which constraint sets apply and what the last check returned, and how editorially complete and mature the record is on a governed scale.

findings.name: Constraint declaration and conformance reporting
findings.description: Which constraint sets are declared applicable at which severity, the outcome of the most recent check against a named record state and constraint version, and what conformance is claimed against external standards.

questions.text: Which constraint sets apply to this concept record, at which severity, and who declared them applicable?
answer_data: Constraint set reference with its version identifier
Declared severity per constraint and the declaring role

questions.text: What did the most recent check return, against which record state and which constraint-set version?
answer_data: Conformance boolean plus per-result focus node, path and severity
Digest of the validated record state and the constraint set version

questions.text: Which failures block publication and which are advisory only?
answer_data: Blocking severity threshold for each registration state
Waiver reference where a blocking failure was accepted

questions.text: What conformance to an external standard is claimed for this record, and on what evidence?
answer_data: Named standard, clause and claim scope
Evidence reference supporting the claim, or an explicit no-claim statement

data_elements.name: Constraint set reference
data_elements.description: Versioned reference to the externally owned constraint or shape set declared applicable.

data_elements.name: Conformance flag
data_elements.description: Whether the validated record state satisfied all constraints above the blocking threshold.

data_elements.name: Result severity
data_elements.description: Severity assigned to an individual validation result, such as violation, warning or informational.

data_elements.name: External conformance claim
data_elements.description: Explicit claim of conformance to a named external standard clause, with its supporting evidence reference.

artifacts.name: Concept validation report
artifacts.description: Retained report returned by an external evaluation of one concept record state against a named constraint-set version, carrying the conformance flag and individual results with focus node, path, source constraint and severity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Concept-scoped serial: concept identifier as scope discriminator plus a never-reused integer sequence dedicated to validation reports; where the evaluating system issues its own run identifier, that authoritative master-system identifier is recorded and takes priority for cross-system correlation.

findings.name: Editorial completeness, maturity and quality measurement
findings.description: Which editorial criteria the record has met, how mature and stable the definition is on a governed scale, which quality dimension each measurement addresses, and when the next editorial review falls due.

questions.text: Which editorial completeness criteria has this record met, and which remain open?
answer_data: Met and unmet criteria lists with the assessing agent
Assessment event time

questions.text: How mature and stable is the definition, expressed on a governed scale?
answer_data: Maturity or term-status code from a governed scale
Expected stability statement for the next release

questions.text: Which quality dimension does each recorded measurement address, and by which metric was it computed?
answer_data: Quality dimension and category references
Metric reference, computed value and unit

questions.text: Who last reviewed the editorial content, and when is the next review due?
answer_data: Last review event time and reviewing agent
Next review due instant and the rule that sets it

data_elements.name: Editorial criteria assessment
data_elements.description: Per-criterion met or unmet result for the record's editorial completeness.

data_elements.name: Definition maturity code
data_elements.description: Governed code for how settled the definition is, distinct from registration status.

data_elements.name: Quality measurement
data_elements.description: A computed value for a named metric addressing a named quality dimension, with its unit and generating activity.

data_elements.name: Next review due
data_elements.description: Instant by which the next editorial review must occur, as RFC 3339 with seconds and offset.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Quality here is a set of dimension-scoped measurements and status codes attached to the record and recomputed on each assessment. They are references into an externally owned metric catalogue plus scalar values; freezing them into an artifact would create a stale parallel copy of measurements whose authoritative form is the live measurement series.

bundles.name: Stewardship, namespace, rights and retention
bundles.description: Who owns and maintains the concept record, who controls the namespace its identifier lives in, and under what rights, access, embargo and retention terms the record and its evidence are held.
bundles.rationale: Persistent identifiers require a named custodian and an explicit persistence commitment, and licence, access rights and rights holder must be stated for reusable data; retention and disposition instructions are carried but executed by the records authority.

layers.name: Ownership, stewardship and namespace authority
layers.description: The owning organisation, the named steward, delegated responsibilities and escalation, and the namespace that mints and guarantees the identifier.

findings.name: Ownership, stewardship and delegation
findings.description: Which organisation owns the record, which named steward maintains it, what is delegated without transferring ownership, how escalation works when a steward is unavailable, and how an ownership transfer is recorded without breaking identifier continuity.

questions.text: Which organisation owns this concept record, and which named steward maintains it?
answer_data: Owning organisation reference and steward reference
Effective period of the stewardship assignment

questions.text: What is the escalation and hand-over path when the steward is unavailable or the role lapses?
answer_data: Ordered escalation contacts with roles

findings.inline_only_rationale: Ownership and stewardship are role-qualified references into an externally owned party model plus effective periods. The party's identity, contact data and organisational lifecycle belong to that model, so this finding carries bindings only and must not materialise a local party document.

findings.name: Identifier and namespace stewardship
findings.description: Which namespace mints the concept identifier, who controls it, what resolution and persistence is committed, how identifiers are minted and prevented from collision or reuse, and what happens if the namespace is transferred or discontinued.

answer_data: Namespace identifier or base IRI
Controlling body reference and its mandate

answer_data: Persistence commitment statement and its end condition, if any
Resolution service reference and expected behaviour for retired identifiers

questions.text: How are identifiers minted, reserved and prevented from collision or reuse across the namespace?

Exclusion register of retired identifiers

questions.text: What happens to identifiers if the namespace is transferred, forked or discontinued?
answer_data: Succession plan and receiving custodian
Redirect or archival commitment for existing identifiers

data_elements.name: Namespace reference
data_elements.description: Identifier or base IRI of the namespace in which the concept identifier is minted.

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme
data_elements.description: Governed scheme of the concept identifier, such as a scheme PURL, DOI, Handle, ARK or locally minted UUID or ULID.

data_elements.name: Persistence commitment
data_elements.description: Stated commitment to keep the identifier resolvable, with its custodian and any end condition.

data_elements.name: Reuse exclusion entry
data_elements.description: Register entry blocking a retired identifier from being minted again for a different meaning.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Namespace stewardship is expressed as references to an externally operated namespace and resolution service plus locally held commitments and exclusion entries. The minting service, resolver configuration and its operational records belong to that service, so no local artifact is declared.

layers.name: Rights, access, embargo, retention and disposition
layers.description: Under what licence and access terms the record and its evidence may be reused, what is embargoed until when, and which retention class and disposition instruction the record carries for execution elsewhere.

findings.name: Licence, access rights and embargo

Rights holder reference

Stated basis for the restriction

Fallback state if the releasing event never occurs

Required review outcome and any minimisation or redaction applied

data_elements.name: Licence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the licence controlling reuse of a record part or evidence item.

data_elements.name: Access rights statement
data_elements.description: Statement of who may access a record part, or an indication of its security status.

data_elements.name: Embargo end
data_elements.description: Instant or releasing event after which embargoed content becomes accessible.

data_elements.name: Personal data or third-party rights flag
data_elements.description: Marks an evidence item as identifying a living person or carrying third-party rights, triggering review before publication.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Licence and access terms are carried as references to externally governed policies plus subject-specific constraint parameters. Policy interpretation, evaluation and enforcement belong to the rights policy model and its evaluator, so this finding holds bindings and flags only and declares no local policy artifact.

findings.name: Retention class, disposition instruction and tombstone

Retention period start event and duration

answer_data: Disposition authority reference
Execution confirmation reference returned to this register

Hold release condition or instant
